questions.q: What makes a screen flow different from the record-triggered flows in Lessons 6-7?
options: It is built around one or more screens a user directly interacts with
It can only ever run once per org
It cannot contain any Data elements
It runs exclusively on a schedule
questions.explain: A screen flow puts a user in the loop; record-triggered flows run automatically with no screen at all.

questions.q: What does a Screen element's Screen Properties pane configure?
options: The org's Stripe billing settings
Label, API name, and navigation options for that screen
The object a record-triggered flow listens to
The flow's Debug output
questions.explain: Screen Properties set a Screen element's own label, API name, and navigation (header/footer) options.

options: A connector between two elements
An individual piece a user sees or interacts with on a screen, like a text box or Display Text
A type of data element
A global constant
questions.explain: Screen components are the individual pieces placed on a Screen element — text boxes, picklists, toggles, Display Text, and more.

questions.q: What does Display Text do, specifically, as a screen component?
options: Shows information to the user with no input required
Deletes a record when clicked
Schedules the flow to run later
Collects a date and time from the user
questions.explain: Display Text is a pure output component — it shows information without collecting any input.

questions.q: What launches a screen flow, per this lesson?
options: A platform event message only
A record being deleted
A user action — a button, quick action, tab, or link — never a record change on its own
A nightly batch job with no user involved
questions.explain: Screen flows need a person in the loop and are launched by a user action, unlike the other flow types in this chapter.
